paper.title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents
paper.central_claim: Reframing memory operations as a learnable and evolvable skill bank - an RL-trained controller selects top-K skills per span, a fixed LLM executor applies them in one pass, and a fixed LLM designer refines/adds skills from hard cases with snapshot rollback - improves task performance over strong memory baselines on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, HotpotQA and ALFWorld and generalizes across datasets and base models.

Appendix A (Tables 4-7 incl. AppWorld, small models, stability)
Appendix B (evaluation details, designer details, ALFWorld training, PPO objective)

evidence.quote: Most Large Language Model (LLM) agent memory systems rely on a small set of static, hand-designed operations for extracting memory.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: memory extraction operations are fixed by hand.

evidence.quote: they hard-code memory behaviors into fixed procedural workflows that interleave heuristics with LLM-mediated extraction and revision, making them brittle under distribution shift
evidence.support_explanation: Stated bottleneck of prior pipelines (citing LightMem et al.); no direct measurement of brittleness in this paper beyond baseline scores.

evidence.quote: Despite this progress, memory management is still largely governed by static, hand-crafted routines for extraction, consolidation, and pruning.
evidence.support_explanation: Closest learning-based neighbours (Memory-R1, Mem-alpha, RL-trained memory managers) are dismissed in one sentence and are not experimental baselines; MemEvolve, Evo-Memory, ReasoningBank are also only discussed in text.

evidence.quote: We start from a minimal set of general-purpose primitives to ensure a stable and functional initialization.
evidence.support_explanation: Skill bank is initialised with four primitives (Insert, Update, Delete, Skip); each skill is a description plus a content specification (text).

evidence.quote: We train the controller with reinforcement learning, using downstream task performance as feedback for its skill selections.
evidence.support_explanation: Controller (three small MLPs) is the only weight-trained component; PPO with Gumbel-Top-K.

evidence.quote: After construction, we evaluate the resulting memory bank on the trace’s memory-dependent training queries and use the resulting task performance as the reward (e.g., F1 or success rate).
evidence.support_explanation: Reward is delayed downstream QA/success score with ground-truth answers, not a self-judged signal.

evidence.quote: MemSkill evolves the skill bank using an LLM-based designer (fixed) that operates periodically during training.
evidence.support_explanation: Designer (the improver) is a fixed LLM with fixed prompts: the improver itself is not edited or improved.

evidence.quote: Each case is query-centric, recording the query along with its ground-truth and metadata
evidence.support_explanation: Designer sees ground-truth answers, retrieved memories and prediction of failed training queries; the designer prompt triages storage vs retrieval vs memory-quality failures.

evidence.quote: Notably, we maintain snapshots of the best-performing skill bank and roll back if an update degrades performance, with early stopping when repeated designer updates fail to improve the training signal.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention gate: best-snapshot rollback and early stopping, both on the training signal.

evidence.quote: we compute the average task reward over the last quarter of training steps within the cycle, and treat this value as the cycle’s score.
evidence.support_explanation: Rollback criterion = tail-average training reward of one 100-step cycle compared with best so far; no statistical test, no disjoint validation split for the commit.

evidence.quote: For the designer, skill evolution is triggered every 100 training steps, with at most 3 skill edits per evolution round.
evidence.support_explanation: Bounded edit budget per round; number of rounds and final bank size are not stated.

evidence.quote: (delete and noop operations are not evolved at this time)
evidence.support_explanation: Delete/Noop skills are frozen; skills are only added or refined, never retired, merged or de-duplicated.

evidence.quote: LoCoMo contains 10 long interaction samples, each paired with roughly 200 training queries on average. We split the dataset by sample into train, validation, and test sets with a 6/2/2 ratio.
evidence.support_explanation: Held-out by conversation, but the LoCoMo test set is about two long conversations (adversarial queries removed), so the main test is small.

evidence.quote: Although the training split is not used for learning in this transfer setting, the validation split is used to tune dataset-specific configurations.
evidence.support_explanation: LongMemEval is zero-shot transfer for the skills but configurations are tuned on its validation split; test is a stratified sample of about 100 examples.

evidence.quote: We first collect expert trajectories from the training split and use them as the corpus for memory or experience construction.
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld memories are built from expert trajectories (privileged demonstrations), not from the agent's own experience; the setting is offline memory construction.

evidence.quote: sample another non-overlapping subset of trajectories from the same type as evaluation cases
evidence.support_explanation: Training-time evaluation cases are disjoint from the experience corpus within each task type; official ALF-Seen/ALF-Unseen are the reported splits.

evidence.quote: We use openai/gpt-oss-120b as the LLM judge
evidence.support_explanation: L-J metric rests on one LLM judge scoring 0/0.5/1; no human agreement check is reported.
LoCoMo F1/L-J, LongMemEval F1/L-J, Avg L-J, ALF-Seen SR/steps, ALF-Unseen SR/steps, ALF avg SR.
Strongest LoCoMo L-J baseline in Table 1 (49.71), so the LoCoMo margin is +4.1 L-J.
On ALFWorld (with in-context demonstrations) the best baselines sit at 77.8 (Mem0, CoN 77.80) vs MemSkill 80.36: a 2.5-point margin on 140 + 134 tasks.
On Qwen LongMemEval CoN has F1 29.19 versus MemSkill 25.29 while L-J is 44.06 vs 60.40: the F1 and judge metrics disagree.
Qwen rows are transfer results (skills/controller trained with LLaMA).

L-J on LoCoMo: random selection, fixed four primitives and refine-only each drop; the fixed-primitive variant (46.50 LLaMA) is below A-MEM 49.71 and MemoryOS 48.64, so the evolved skills carry the margin. Single run, LoCoMo only.

evidence.quote: Disabling the designer yields an even larger degradation, especially under Qwen
evidence.support_explanation: Author reading of Table 2.

evidence.quote: Since MemSkill learns and evolves the skill bank before deployment, this preparation cost is amortized over repeated use, with further evolution triggered only occasionally.
evidence.support_explanation: Only inference-time cost is reported; PPO training, designer calls, rollout cost and A6000 hours are not quantified.

Inference tokens/calls are well reported and favour MemSkill; quality is non-monotonic in span size (SS=1024 falls below A-MEM/MemoryOS), so span granularity is a large unablated confound for the reported margins.

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise specified, we use K = 7 K{=}7 skills for LoCoMo and LongMemEval at evaluation time, and K = 5 K{=}5 for ALFWorld.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation selects 7 of the ~9 listed LoCoMo skills and 5 of ~7 ALFWorld skills.

evidence.quote: and the controller selects K = 3 K{=}3 skills per unit
evidence.support_explanation: Training uses K=3 but evaluation K=7; text states K=7 is best on HotpotQA curves, so K is effectively tuned on reported results.

evidence.quote: Evolved Skill on LoCoMo - REFINE_TEMPORAL_DETAILS_WITH_CONTEXT
evidence.support_explanation: Appendix C lists nine LoCoMo skills (four primitives, two of them rewritten, plus five new: activity details, entity nuances, temporal context, entity relationships, temporal refinement); the paper says it shows representative skills so final bank size is not given.

evidence.quote: Evolved Skill on ALFWorld - TRACK_OBJECT_MOVEMENTS
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld listing has seven skills (primitives plus action constraints, object location, object movements): domain-specialised, small bank.

evidence.quote: MemSkill consistently outperforms strong baselines such as MemoryOS and A-MEM, with gains becoming more pronounced in the challenging long-context setting.
evidence.support_explanation: HotpotQA transfer claim relies on Fig 3 bars (not readable) and compares only MemoryOS and A-MEM.

evidence.quote: With LLaMA, the No-Memory baseline already performs strongly, indicating that in-context demonstrations provide substantial task-specific guidance and make this setting partially saturated.
evidence.support_explanation: AppWorld (with demonstrations): MemSkill avg PR 47.32 vs No-Memory 46.41 and AWM 47.11.
Second group of columns (with demonstrations): 47.32 average pass rate.
AWM within 0.21 of MemSkill under demonstrations; no-demonstration gap is 1.3 points; AppWorld training details for MemSkill are not given in Appendix B.

evidence.quote: If the updated skill bank underperforms the best-performing snapshot observed so far, we roll back to the best snapshot and continue subsequent evolution from it.
evidence.support_explanation: Rollback semantics: subsequent evolution continues from the best snapshot (versioning kept in memory).

evidence.quote: the learned skills show clear domain specialization.
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative support that evolved skills encode dataset-specific needs (temporal/activity for LoCoMo, constraints/locations for ALFWorld).

evidence.quote: MemSkill consistently achieves the best performance across both base models and evaluation splits.
evidence.support_explanation: Additional ALFWorld baselines LightMem, AWM, ExpeL (Table 4): LLaMA avg 80.36 vs LightMem 74.83; Qwen avg 81.29 vs ExpeL 73.68.

signatures.object: Skill bank: structured text skills (description + content: purpose, when to use, how to apply, constraints, action type), baseline = four hand-written primitives Insert/Update/Delete/Skip
signatures.information: Designer sees clustered, difficulty-ranked failed training queries with ground truth, retrieved memories, prediction and failure counts; it is told to triage storage vs retrieval vs memory-quality failure; no test data
signatures.operation: Two-stage LLM analysis then up to 3 add_new/refine_existing skill edits every 100 training steps; only insert/update-type skills are evolvable
signatures.output: New or rewritten skill texts (e.g. capture temporal context, track object location)
signatures.conditions: Ground-truth answers for training queries; hard-case buffer with age/capacity expiry; exploration bias toward new skills for 50 steps
signatures.feedback: Downstream F1/success of the memory built with the skill set on memory-dependent training queries
signatures.selection_rule_data: Cycle score = tail-quarter mean training reward; roll back to best snapshot if not improved; early stop after patience; selection reuses the training distribution (no disjoint validation)
signatures.persistence: Shared skill bank across traces; snapshots of the best bank
signatures.later_use: Controller scores skills via description embedding; executor applies selected skills at test time on unseen traces
signatures.claimed_effect: Removing the designer (fixed primitives) lowers LoCoMo L-J 53.82 to 46.50 (LLaMA) and 54.14 to 36.15 (Qwen)
signatures.failure_boundary: No retirement/merge/dedup; delete/noop frozen; designer fixed; final bank size, rounds and cost unreported

signatures.object: Controller: MLP state-skill scorer that picks an ordered Top-K subset of skills per text span (weights trained)
signatures.information: Embedding of current span and mean embedding of retrieved memories, and skill description embeddings; reward only after the whole memory bank is built
signatures.operation: PPO with joint Top-K probability, value function, entropy bonus, Gumbel-Top-K sampling
signatures.output: Skill subset passed to the fixed LLM executor, which writes memory actions in one pass per span
signatures.conditions: Variable-size bank handled by shared scorer; trained with K=3, evaluated with K=7 (LoCoMo/LongMemEval) or 5 (ALFWorld)
signatures.feedback: Episode-level reward (F1 or success rate) from memory-dependent training queries
signatures.persistence: Controller weights; transferred to Qwen, LongMemEval and HotpotQA without retraining
signatures.later_use: Used at inference on test traces
signatures.claimed_effect: Random skill selection lowers LoCoMo L-J (53.82 to 48.43 LLaMA, 54.14 to 42.84 Qwen)
signatures.failure_boundary: With 7 of ~9 skills selected the controller mostly excludes two skills; reward credit is delayed and episode-level

signatures.object: Memory construction granularity: span-level one-pass skill-conditioned extraction instead of turn-by-turn LLM calls
signatures.information: Fixed-length token spans (default 512) plus retrieved memories
signatures.operation: Compose several selected skills in one LLM call per span
signatures.output: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE blocks applied to the trace memory bank
signatures.conditions: Span size is a cost/quality knob
signatures.selection_rule_data: SS=512 chosen as best balance on LoCoMo
signatures.persistence: Trace-specific memory bank (built per trace, not retained across traces)
signatures.later_use: Retrieval of up to 20 memory items for answering
signatures.claimed_effect: Fewer tokens and LLM calls than MemoryOS, A-MEM and LightMem at higher L-J
signatures.failure_boundary: SS=1024 yields 48.11 L-J; the granularity effect is not ablated for baselines

gap.author_gap: Agent memory systems use static hand-designed operations (add/update/delete/skip), fixed per-turn units and heuristic modules, making them rigid under diverse interaction patterns and inefficient on long histories.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and non-trivial (the fixed object is the memory-extraction operation set, and the fixed-primitive ablation shows it is a real bottleneck: 46.50 vs 53.82 L-J). The brittleness-under-shift premise is argued by citation rather than measured here.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Ancestors in local text: MemoryBank, A-MEM, Mem0, MemoryOS, LightMem (fixed pipelines); learning-based neighbours Memory-R1 and Mem-alpha (RL-trained memory management) and concurrent Evo-Memory, MemEvolve, ReasoningBank, ExpeL, EvolveR, SkillWeaver, ADAS. Experimental baselines cover the first group plus AWM/ExpeL on ALFWorld/AppWorld, not Memory-R1/Mem-alpha/MemEvolve (version 2 text, originals absent).
gap.residue: Learned or evolving memory operations compared with other learned memory managers; gains separated from the span-level granularity change; evolution cost.
gap.stakes: Long-history conversational and embodied agents where fixed extraction misses task-relevant details and costs many LLM calls.
gap.method_response: Skills are text routines selected by an RL controller; a designer rewrites/adds them from hard cases under a rollback guard.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether gains hold against RL-trained memory managers and against a granularity-matched baseline, variance across runs, and how many designer rounds are needed.
unresolved: Closest RL-memory neighbours' originals not in package
Final skill bank sizes and number of evolution rounds

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Definition match: a conventionally fixed component of a staged procedure (hand-designed memory extraction operations and per-turn granularity) is treated as a free design variable and redesigned (learnable skills, span-level one-pass). Sub-cards C15/C23/C24 concern 3D representations, diffusion chain internals and diffusion conditioning interfaces and do not apply, hence sub null.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: liberated component named with reason (met: hand-crafted ops), ablation reverts to the standard form (met: w/o Des), no retraining of the executor LLM (met). Failure: strongest baseline omitted (partly: RL-memory managers absent), several modules changed at once (controller, designer, span-level granularity) with the granularity not ablated.
matches.reason: The central move is making a fixed pipeline component learnable and evolvable; the tactic cards in this parent do not match so no sub-card.

rs_pattern.reason: Single primary assigned; no second distinct operation needing another main card (controller RL and designer editing are domain-layer operations).
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: the fixed-primitive bottleneck is shown by the w/o Des ablation on LoCoMo; generality of the claim over other learned memory managers and across tasks is not closed.

condition_checks.reason: Failures are clustered by query/error type before the designer proposes edits.
Rollback to the best snapshot protects earlier gains, but only failures are fed to the designer and the commit test is the training reward.
Validation signal is ground-truth task reward, not self-constructed.
Edits are re-evaluated by subsequent training and kept if the tail reward improves; no disjoint validation split for the commit.
Designer, executor and ground-truth reward are the stated fixed anchors.
Comparison against the fixed hand-designed primitive set (w/o Des) is reported.
Cost of search/evolution is not reported.
No variance across runs or seeds; small LoCoMo test.
Transfer to other datasets/models shown against baselines, but not against a universal seed design nor with variance.
Reward comes from downstream QA/success after the memory has been built, not from the construction episode itself.
Reader/executor LLMs are frozen and not co-trained with the controller.
The trained policy is a skill selector, not the memory writer itself - pattern at the edge.

revision_proposals: Skill bank designed as editable text with a learned selector sits across H11 (skill revision) and H26 (trained curator); no single card captures 'evolve the operation set + learn to select it'. Note as a candidate case, not a card edit.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: turn a conventionally fixed pipeline component into a designed variable; domain: revise skill documents from attributed failures with bounded edits. MemSkill's designer rewrites and adds the memory-operation skills (the formerly hand-fixed component) from clustered failures under an edit budget and rollback.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_differences: RS requires an ablation that reverts to the fixed component (met: w/o Des); H11 requires defect-vs-lapse separation and disjoint validation for retention (partial: triage of storage/retrieval/quality failure, but commit uses training reward).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: the fixed component redesigned is the memory extraction procedure; domain H21: an outer loop redesigns the inner agent's learning mechanism. The designer loop edits that mechanism; the executor and the designer stay fixed.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_differences: H21 expects design-selection data kept out of reported benchmarks and a universal-seed baseline; here training/test splits are disjoint but there is no universal seed comparison or variance.

claims.text: MemSkill improves over strong memory baselines on LoCoMo, LongMemEval and ALFWorld.
claims.setting: LLaMA-3.3-70B (trained) and Qwen3-Next-80B (transfer), API-accessed; LoCoMo/LongMemEval conversational QA and ALFWorld with demonstrations; retrieve up to 20 memories for all methods
claims.baseline_control: No-Memory, CoN, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, A-MEM, Mem0, LangMem, MemoryOS; additional LightMem, AWM, ExpeL
claims.selection_vs_test: LoCoMo split by conversation 6/2/2, ALFWorld official splits, LongMemEval transfer sample about 100; rollback chosen on training reward
claims.result_denominator: LoCoMo L-J 53.82 vs 49.71 (A-MEM); LongMemEval L-J 60.89 vs 56.44 (CoN); ALF avg SR 80.36 vs 77.82; single run, no intervals
claims.allowed_conclusion: On the tested benchmarks MemSkill scores higher than the compared memory baselines by roughly 2-5 points on main metrics; magnitude is uncertain (single run, small test sets) and F1/L-J disagree on Qwen LongMemEval.

claims.text: Both learning skill selection and evolving the skill bank matter.
claims.setting: LoCoMo L-J ablation on LLaMA and Qwen
claims.baseline_control: w/o Ctrl (random), w/o Des (four primitives), refine-only
claims.allowed_conclusion: On LoCoMo, evolving the bank (designer) gives the larger gain; the controller's gain is measured against random choice of 7 out of about 9 skills.

claims.text: Learned skills generalize across datasets and base models.
claims.setting: LoCoMo-trained skills to LongMemEval and HotpotQA; LLaMA-trained to Qwen
claims.baseline_control: baselines run on target data (MemoryOS, A-MEM on HotpotQA only)
claims.selection_vs_test: no training on targets; LongMemEval validation split tunes configs
claims.allowed_conclusion: Skills transfer between conversational QA sets and across two large LLMs; HotpotQA magnitude cannot be verified from text.

claims.text: Span-level skill-conditioned construction is more efficient than turn-level baselines.
claims.setting: LoCoMo with LLaMA, inference-time tokens and calls
claims.result_denominator: SS=512: 53.82 L-J, 249K input tokens, 215 calls vs A-MEM 49.71, 2850K, 1548
claims.allowed_conclusion: Inference cost is far lower; training and evolution cost are excluded.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A skill bank evolved by an LLM designer from training-set failures, plus an RL skill selector, yields higher LoCoMo/LongMemEval L-J and ALFWorld success than the compared memory pipelines on held-out conversations/tasks and transfers to other datasets and a second LLM; the improver itself is fixed and cost, variance and RL-memory-manager baselines are missing.
assessment.level_reason: Retained skill bank and controller are evaluated on held-out traces and other datasets (EVIDENCE retained); designer is fixed so no improver-level claim.

G.reason: Names the fixed object (hand-designed memory operations/granularity) with a measured bottleneck (w/o Des) and lists many neighbours, but the most relevant learned-memory neighbours are not compared and brittleness is cited, not measured.

M.reason: Coherent, reconstructable mechanism (reward from downstream QA, failure triage, clustered hard cases, bounded edits, exploration for new skills) with a distinguishable prediction (fixed primitives lose); caveats are span-granularity confound and a selector over a small bank.

X.reason: Retention is explicit: edit cap per round, snapshots, best-snapshot rollback, early stopping and hard-case expiry, with the next-round reading by controller/executor; however the commit test is the training reward with no disjoint validation, no skill retirement/merge, delete/noop frozen, bank size and rounds not given.

E.measurement.reason: Programmatic ALFWorld success plus F1 and judge-scored QA on public benchmarks, with a stated protocol; the single unvalidated judge and F1/L-J disagreement on Qwen LongMemEval lower confidence, and ALFWorld memory is built from expert trajectories.

E.causality.reason: No-memory control, random-selection, fixed-primitive and refine-only ablations on two LLMs, no-demonstration ALFWorld control and extra baselines; missing: RL-memory-manager baselines, granularity-matched baseline, ablations beyond LoCoMo, and repeats.

E.holdout.reason: LoCoMo split by conversation, official ALF-Seen/Unseen, zero-shot transfer to LongMemEval/HotpotQA and a second LLM; limited by tiny test sets, validation-tuned dataset configs, K chosen on reported curves and training-reward rollback.

E.statistics.reason: Dataset sizes and per-metric rows are given but there are no seeds, intervals or tests; margins of 2-5 points on about two conversations, about 100 LongMemEval items and 140/134 ALFWorld tasks cannot be judged; AppWorld margins are 0.2-1.3.

E.cost.reason: Inference tokens, calls and quality are tabulated across span sizes and three baselines, but training, designer and PPO cost (the part that matters for the evolve claim) are excluded as 'amortized'.

rationale: Sound skill-bank evolution with held-out transfer; single runs, small tests, fixed designer, training cost and RL-memory baselines missing.
